8.text: 🇷🇺 Video of grandfather's wartime heroism inspires marine to join special military operation A video depicting the heroic actions of a grandfather during wartime motivated a Russian marine to enlist in the special military operation. The footage, shared widely online, highlighted personal sacrifice and patriotism. The marine cited the video as a key factor in his decision to serve. Source: RIA Novosti

9.text: 🔥 Russian strikes hit dual-use warehouse and energy infrastructure in Ukraine Russia's Armed Forces continue carrying out group strikes on logistics centers, port and energy infrastructure of Ukraine used in the interests of the Ukrainian Armed Forces. Among the targets hit were a warehouse storing dual-use goods and energy facilities. • Targets included logistics centers, port and energy infrastructure • A warehouse storing dual-use goods was struck • Strikes continue as part of ongoing group operations Source: TASS

5.text: ⚠️ Nearly 80 Ukrainian drones destroyed over Bryansk region in 24 hours Russia's defense ministry reported that almost 80 Ukrainian drones were destroyed over Bryansk region during a 24-hour period. No further details were provided about damage or casualties on the ground. Source: RIA Novosti

12.text: 🏛️ FT lists possible reasons China blocked G20 communique The Financial Times has outlined possible reasons why China blocked the G20 communique. Details of the reported reasons were not provided in the source. Source: RIA Novosti

13.text: ⚖️ Russia's Supreme Court protects 89-year-old pensioner who lost only home Russia's Supreme Court has ruled in defense of an 89-year-old pensioner who was deprived of his only housing. The ruling overturns prior decisions that had left the elderly man without a home. Source: RIA Novosti

14.text: 🚗 Cold water floods roadway in northern Saint Petersburg A roadway in the north of Saint Petersburg was flooded with cold water, local authorities reported. Specialists are already working to address the aftermath of the incident. • Location is in the northern part of Saint Petersburg • Repair crews are on site Source: TASS

15.text: 🧑‍⚖️ Almost half of world’s farmers poisoned by pesticides annually, study finds A new study estimates 402–433 million cases of unintentional acute pesticide poisoning among farmers and farm workers each year. Pesticide poisoning kills around 11,000 people annually, with India accounting for nearly 60% of fatalities, according to data from 2006–2023. • Study commissioned by Pesticide Action Network • 11,000 deaths per year linked to pesticide poisoning Source: The Guardian

16.text: 💰 VEB.RF backed four investment projects worth 130 billion rubles Kerefov announced that VEB.RF has supported four investment projects totaling 130 billion rubles. The statement was reported by Vedomosti. No further details on the specific projects were provided. Source: Vedomosti

17.text: 🌐 Israeli forces and settlers attack two West Bank mosques Israeli forces fired tear gas into one mosque in the West Bank after settlers set fire to and vandalised another. The separate incidents reflect ongoing tensions between settlers and Palestinian residents in the occupied territory. • Settlers set fire to and vandalised one mosque • Israeli forces fired tear gas into another mosque • Both incidents occurred in the West Bank Source: Al Jazeera

18.text: 🔥 Iran strikes US bases in Middle East after reports of US attack on wedding party Iran has attacked US bases in the Middle East following reports that a US strike killed five people at a wedding party. The Iranian Red Crescent says a child was among those killed when shrapnel from a US strike hit a home. The US military says it is aware of the reports and never targets civilians. • Iranian Red Crescent says a child was killed by shrapnel from a US strike on a home • Reports say a US strike killed five people at a wedding party • US military says it is aware of the reports and never targets civilians Source: BBC

19.text: 🏛️ Republican senator urges Trump to fire Defence Secretary Hegseth Senator Thom Tillis has called on President Donald Trump to remove Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of 'inept mismanagement' of the Pentagon. The demand comes as the US military faces strain from the ongoing war on Iran. • Tillis is a Republican senator • Hegseth leads the Pentagon Source: Al Jazeera

20.text: ⚠️ Iranian attack on Saudi tanker killed two Filipino sailors, Saudi Arabia says Saudi Arabia says two Filipino crew members were killed in an Iranian attack on the tanker Sidr in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. The kingdom condemned the targeting of the vessel, which was reportedly hit by unknown projectiles. • Tanker Sidr reportedly hit by unknown projectiles • Saudi Arabia condemned the attack • Two Filipino sailors killed Source: BBC

21.text: ⚖️ Arktikugol trust to challenge arrest of Russian ship in Svalbard The Arktikugol trust will challenge Norway's decision to arrest the Russian research vessel Professor Molchanov at the request of Ukrainian company Naftogaz, Russian Minister for the Development of the Far East and Arctic Alexei Chekunkov said at a session of the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok on Thursday. • Norwegian authorities ordered the arrest at Naftogaz's request • Chekunkov spoke on the sidelines of the Eastern Economic Forum Source: Interfax

22.text: 🏛️ Lavrov calls European Commission head a 'Führer' Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has publicly labelled the head of the European Commission a 'Führer', according to Lenta.ru. The statement was reported on Monday; no further details were provided in the source. Source: Lenta.ru

23.text: 🏛️ Putin calls for making the Far East a center of economic growth Russian President Vladimir Putin has called for turning the Far East into a hub of economic growth. The statement was made as part of the region's development strategy. Source: Lenta.ru

24.text: 🤝 Russia will continue to support Iran, Peskov says Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated that Russia will continue to support Iran. He did not elaborate on the forms or timing of the assistance. Source: RIA Novosti

25.text: ⛽ Putin says 90% of Russian refineries repaired after drone attacks caused fuel disruptions Russian President Vladimir Putin said domestic companies have repaired 90% of the country's oil refineries damaged in recent attacks, with only 10% still under repair. He noted that Russian firms showed 'a sense of responsibility' amid fuel supply disruptions. • Only 10% of refineries remain to be repaired • Putin praised companies' 'sense of responsibility' Source: TASS

26.text: ⚖️ Victims sue South African government over 1961 Sharpeville massacre Victims of the infamous apartheid-era Sharpeville massacre have filed a lawsuit against the South African government. The shooting on 21 March 1960 left 91 dead after protesters gathered to demonstrate against pass laws. The claim is part of a broader wave of litigation for apartheid-era crimes. • 91 people killed in the Sharpeville shooting on 21 March 1960 • Protesters marched against pass laws forcing Black, Indian and Coloured South Africans to carry… • March organized by the Pan Africanist Congress (PAC), a breakaway from the ANC Source: The Guardian

27.text: 🗳️ Russia–Arab World summit could be held in 2027, says Kobyakov Russian presidential aide Boris Kobyakov said a Russia–Arab World summit may be held in 2027. No exact date or venue has been set so far. Source: Vedomosti

28.text: 🏆 Hugh Jackman eyes Norwich City purchase to rival Ryan Reynolds's Wrexham Actor Hugh Jackman, known for playing Wolverine opposite Ryan Reynolds's Deadpool, is reportedly targeting a takeover of Championship side Norwich City. The move would set up a Hollywood derby between the two actors' clubs, following Reynolds's celebrated 2020 purchase of Wrexham. • Reynolds and fellow actor Rob McElhenney bought Wrexham in 2020 • Norwich currently play in the Championship • Jackman and Reynolds co-starred in the Deadpool and Wolverine films Source: Al Jazeera

29.text: 🤝 Burnham, Macron meet to discuss border security and stronger UK-Europe ties New UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham held his first official meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron. The two leaders discussed shared challenges and the prospect of stronger ties between the UK and Europe, including border security. • Topics included shared challenges and border security • It was Burnham's first official meeting as prime minister Source: Al Jazeera
